content.text:
I submitted index 83 (Fe 0.62, Ni 0.22, V 0.16) as the best composition. It gave 1.5×10⁻⁷ A under 2.4 eV light. That's low in absolute terms, and I can't tell how it compares with the library's best, since I measured only 3 of the 200 candidates.

| Index | Composition (Fe / Ni / V) | Why I picked it | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 99 | 0.41 / 0.18 / 0.41 | Close to FeVO4, a known photoanode that absorbs visible light | 0 A |
| 83 | 0.62 / 0.22 / 0.16 | Fe-rich, likely hematite-like with a gap near 2.1 eV | 1.5×10⁻⁷ A |
| 3 | 0.15 / 0.17 / 0.68 | V-rich, likely V2O5-like, a region the library samples heavily | −1×10⁻⁸ A (effectively zero) |

- **Budget:** all 3 photocurrent measurements are spent. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so I never checked which crystal phases are actually present.
- **Model results:** they didn't guide the choices much. MACE puts FeVO4 on the convex hull, and MEGNet gives it a band gap of 2.08 eV (PBE) or 2.75 eV (HSE). Even so, the FeVO4-like film gave no photocurrent.
- **Not explored:** I never measured the Ni-rich region, and index 83 is the only Fe-rich point I measured. The best composition in the library could be in either area.
